title: ServerOS relations sidecar row
description: One line of the derived relations index. The index is a PROJECTION: it can
be deleted and rebuilt from canonical objects at any time, and it is never
the only place a relation is stored. The `derived_from` field is what makes
that checkable — every row must name the canonical object that already
carries the relation, so a row whose source disappears is detectable as a

from.description: Typed locator of the subject object, e.g. item:LIT-0101

rel.description: Closed set. A relation outside it is not expressible here.

to.description: Typed locator of the object, e.g. project:litellm

description: Canonical locators this row was computed from. NOT a provenance nicety:
it is the assertion that the relation already exists somewhere other
than this file. A row with no derivable source must not be written.
